new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. Ударение отсутствует. Имеется четыре уровневых т о н а: ультравысокий (уВ) — a̋, высокий (В) — á, низкий (Н) — à, ультранизкий (уН) — ȁ. Носителем тона является каждая гласная и «слоговая» согласная /ŋ/. Тональные различия используются не только в лексических, но и в грамматических целях, например: ɗő ‛идти’ → ɗó ‛идти (в хабитуалисе)’ (см. 2.3.5.).
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. There is no stress. There are four level tones: extra-high (a̋), high (á), low (à), extra-low (ȁ). The tone-bearing unit is every vowel and the 'syllabic' consonant /ŋ/. Tonal distinctions are used not only for lexical but also for grammatical purposes, e.g. ɗő 'go' → ɗó 'go (habitual)' (see 2.3.5).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tura is a four-level tone language with no word stress; prosodic organisation is by tone over vowels/syllabic ŋ within a phonological word (the authors reject the syllable as a useful unit, 2.1.4), with only three marginal phrase-intonation contours.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none (no stress at all per source)
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Related prosody: the Waalu-Kulukoro contact dialect has three tones instead of four (1.2.1); 'expressive' intonation raises tones and lengthens the initial consonant of a highlighted stretch but 'practically does not affect overall intensity' (2.1.2, p. 590).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the language's word prosody in general (section 'Ударение' slot of the Jazyki Mira template); description based on the Nao dialect (2.0.0), drawing on Bearth 1971 and Idiatov's fieldwork. Bearth 1971 itself (also saved) describes prosody purely in terms of tone, moras and demarcative junctures and has no accent section, consistent with but not explicitly stating absence of stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Both sources describe the Nao (нао) dialect of Tura/Toura (tour1242, ISO neb); Idiatov & Aplonova note that all existing grammatical descriptions of Tura treat only Nao, and that the Waalu-Kulukoro contact dialect has three rather than four tones. Language names: Toura (Fr.), Tura, Wen/Ween; autonym wɛ̃̀ɛ̃̀.

(no stress); four level tones (extra-high, high, low, extra-low), tone borne by every vowel and syllabic /ŋ/; 2.1.4 argues syllable structure is not a useful notion, the relevant unit is the phonological word ('macro-syllable'); phrase intonation limited to three contours. sources.note: Part II Phonologie pp. 11-77 (TOC read; ch. 4 Les tons p. 45 'le toura est une langue à tons ponctuels', four registers, mora = tone-bearing duration unit; ch. 6 mot phonologique, 6.4 p. 68 'Le mot phonologique comme unité rythmique' = a duration unit counted in moras with demarcative features; ch. 7 intonation and final tone sandhi). No accent/stress section and no statement about stress found (scanned grep for accent/intensité plus page images of pp. 68-69); 'accent' occurs only in note 1 as the name of the tone diacritics. Silent on word stress.

sources.note: Family-level: 'Ударение в большинстве М.я. отсутствует. Там, где оно может быть выделено (в частности, бамана), его функциональная нагрузка невелика.' (Stress is absent in most Mande languages; where identifiable, e.g. Bamana, low functional load.) Not Tura-specific.
